dict.string: Set system volume with a keyword and a percentage.

Type your keyword followed by a whole number from 0 to 100, then press Return. The default keyword is vol.
Examples: vol 25, vol 50, vol 100. vol 0 silences and mutes; positive values unmute.
To change the keyword, open Alfred Preferences → Workflows → Volume Control → Configure Workflow, then edit Keyword. For example, set it to sound and use sound 50.
Sets the current macOS output device. Cached NSAppleScript runs inside Alfred, avoiding a shell or a new interpreter process for each command. The compiled-script cache is enabled. No downloads, background service, or additional dependencies.
In a local test, the cached action took about 45 ms in Alfred. First use and other audio devices may take longer. This measures action execution time, not keyboard-to-speaker latency.
Invalid inputs return an error notification without changing volume. Successful changes are silent. Requires Alfred 5 with Powerpack. Outputs whose volume is fixed by hardware (some HDMI, USB, and digital devices) cannot be adjusted by macOS.
The complete script is editable in the Run NSAppleScript action.
Alfred documentation: https://www.alfredapp.com/help/workflows/actions/run-nsapplescript/
Author: -LAN- License: MIT Source: https://github.com/laipz8200/alfred-volume-control
Type this before the percentage, e.g. vol 50 or sound 50.
Enter a whole number from 0 to 100

on alfred_script(q) if q is "" or (count q) > 3 then return "Enter a whole number from 0 to 100." repeat with c in characters of q if c is not in "0123456789" then return "Enter a whole number from 0 to 100." end repeat set level to q as integer if level > 100 then return "Enter a whole number from 0 to 100." try set volume output volume level output muted (level is 0) return "" on error messageText return "Could not set volume: " & messageText end try end alfred_script
